questions.question: [NEET 2021 | Biology] The primary CO\u₂₀₈₂ acceptor in the C₃ (Calvin) cycle is:
questions.solution: # Answer: **(B) RuBP (Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate)** ## Step-by-Step Explanation ### The Calvin Cycle (C₃ Cycle) Overview The Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma of chloroplasts and consists of 3 phases: 1. **Carbon Fixation** ✓ 2. Reduction 3. Regeneration ### The Carbon Fixation Step (First Phase) **The primary CO₂ acceptor is RuBP:** ``` CO₂ + RuBP (5-carbon) ↓ [RuBisCO enzyme] 2 × 3-PGA (3-carbon molecules) ``` - **RuBP** combines with atmospheric CO₂ - This reaction is catalyzed by **RuBisCO** (ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase) - The product immediately splits into two molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate (3-PGA) ### Why It's Called "C₃ Cycle" The very first stable product formed is **3-PGA** (a 3-carbon compound), which is why it's called the **C₃ cycle**. --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong | Option | Why Wrong | |--------|-----------| | **(A) OAA** | OAA is the primary CO₂ acceptor in **C₄ photosynthesis**, not C₃ | | **(C) PEP** | PEP combines with CO₂ in C₄ plants (forming OAA), not in C₃ | | **(D) Pyruvate** | Pyruvate is not involved as a CO₂ acceptor in the Calvin cycle | --- ## Key Formula to Remember **RuBP + CO₂ → (via RuBisCO) → 2 × 3-PGA** This is the cornerstone reaction of photosynthesis that captures atmospheric carbon!
